source.title: Topological Signatures of Grokking
source.authors: Yi-Fan Tang; Qi-Quan Wang; Inés García-Redondo; Anthea Monod

record.tranche_reason: Trains models on modular addition and measures train/test accuracy to examine delayed generalization, using different architectures and a modified setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports label-permutation ablations and PH–accuracy correlations across layers and permutation levels. The correlation tables are not expanded into separate rows because they do not measure the algorithmic circuit or its removal; the text’s directly relevant aggregate and timing results are recorded below. Fourier plots are included because they report the evolution of frequencies and their relationship to test accuracy.
record.test_reason: Trains Transformers and MLPs on modular addition at several primes and training fractions and reports train/test accuracy curves. Test generalization follows fast memorization, with a delay that grows as the training fraction shrinks, which is the original grokking setup and measure. Most of the paper is about persistent-homology (PH) diagnostics, which do not map onto a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state that improvements in test accuracy precede the PH transition in the Transformer by about 1,000 steps, but occur roughly simultaneously in the MLP. They note that PH gives descriptive, not mechanistic, summaries.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition and train/test accuracy to examine grokking, but uses two-token inputs, its own Transformer and MLP architectures, and persistent-homology analyses; the Fourier comparison is for one representative run.
record.method_sensitivity: The delay depends on training fraction: the Transformer generalizes later at α = 0.2 than α = 0.3. Increasing label permutation weakens or eliminates grokking and its associated PH patterns. PH behavior differs by architecture, layer, prime, and task; MNIST has no sharp H1 transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer: changes in test accuracy precede changes in PH statistics (e.g., total H0 persistence) by about 1,000 steps. MLP: peak cross-correlation is near zero lag (Appendix C.2, Fig. 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topological reorganization of embeddings lags or coincides with grokking rather than anticipating it.

fits_no_version.finding: H1 maximum and total persistence of embeddings and hidden layers rise at grokking in both Transformer and MLP. The layer-3 pattern depends on the prime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking on modular arithmetic coincides with emergence of a dominant persistent 1-cycle in representations.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, H1 persistence shows no sharp transition and no dominant cycle.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topological grokking signatures depend on the task having cyclic latent structure.

fits_no_version.finding: With ≥20% permuted training labels, the Transformer fails to generalize within 60k steps, and PH–accuracy correlations collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label corruption above about 20% prevents grokking within a fixed budget.

record.problems: The paper reports exact grokking timings in text for only two Transformer training fractions; many other plotted outcomes are described qualitatively. The Fourier analysis is one representative run. MNIST initialization-scale values and exact accuracy outcomes are not stated. The study does not identify or causally test a memorizing circuit or its removal.
record.rows_left_out: The detailed Transformer and MLP PH–test-accuracy correlation tables and additional label-permutation plots in Appendix C are not expanded into separate rows; they report layer-by-layer correlations rather than measurements of the algorithmic circuit named in V2. Other-prime plots are not entered as numeric rows because the text does not state their accuracy timings or numerical persistence values.

untested.parts: Exact delays for p = 113 and p = 149 and for α = 0.25 are not given in text. Test accuracy reaching near-perfect is implied by 'confirm the grokking pattern' but not quantified.
Whether progress measures anticipate the jump (the restricted/excluded Fourier curves are only said to 'track'). Removal of memorizing components. Identification of the full circuit.
Untested in effect: the MNIST initialization-scale sweep has no stated values or delay comparison. Text, molecules and weight-norm interventions are not studied.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not tested: weight decay fixed at 0.1; no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Not tested: algorithms learned across runs are not compared.
Not tested: AdamW only; no optimizer or floating-point controls.

missing.what: MLP cross-correlation result: peak at near-zero lag between test-accuracy changes and PH statistics (contrasts with the Transformer's lag).
Local intrinsic dimension rises to about 20–25 during memorization and drops sharply to about 5 at the grokking step.
MNIST train/test accuracy for each initialization scale α, needed to judge any grokking-like delay.

record.verdict_notes: Most of the paper's contribution is PH diagnostics, which do not correspond to any claim version; those rows are re-linked to 'none' and logged under fits_no_version. The V3 verdict is withheld because the MNIST text gives no initialization-dependent delay. The V2 support is weak: it rests on one qualitative, single-run Fourier observation.

versions.untested_parts: The explicitly quantified delay comparison is for p = 197 and the Transformer. Other prime results are described as consistent but their timing values are not stated in text.

The paper does not test removal of memorizing components or identify a complete generalizing circuit. Its Fourier analysis is reported for one representative run, and the PH timing analysis concerns representation statistics.

MNIST is tested with varying initialization scales, but the text does not state their values or show that initialization switches grokking on or off. Weight-norm interventions, text, molecules, and other non-algorithmic settings are not tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
Weight decay is fixed; the study does not test an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
Only AdamW is used; optimizer instability and floating-point or softmax artifacts are not tested or controlled by comparison.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition with progressively permuted training labels.
rows.measure: Test accuracy and whether grokking occurs
rows.baseline: Low-permutation conditions grok within the same training budget.
rows.value: The model did not generalize within 60,000 steps and remained in a memorization-dominated regime with high training accuracy and poor out-of-sample performance.
rows.note: This is a deliberately corrupted-label condition.
rows.check: A deliberately corrupted-label control (Pfrac ≥ 20%). V1 concerns clean algorithmic data and makes no claim about label noise, so this row bears on no version.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track the token-embedding Fourier spectrum during modular-addition training.
rows.measure: Concentration of the token-embedding Fourier spectrum
rows.value: The spectrum progressively concentrates around a small number of dominant frequencies.
rows.note: This reports gradual frequency concentration, but does not establish that memorizing components are removed.
rows.check: The text says the embedding Fourier spectrum 'progressively concentrates' over training, which is the gradual-formation part of V2. This is one representative run, described qualitatively. Memorization removal is untested, but that belongs under untested parts, not in the row state.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compare test accuracy with accuracies restricted to or excluding dominant Fourier frequencies.
rows.measure: Test accuracy, restricted accuracy, and excluded accuracy
rows.value: Restricted and excluded accuracies closely track test accuracy; numerical values are figure-only.
rows.note: The paper describes the curves as tracking one another; it does not report numerical values in text.
rows.check: Figure-only. The text says restricted and excluded accuracies 'closely track' test accuracy and gives no lead or lag, so the row cannot show whether these measures anticipate the jump.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Cross-correlate first-order differences in test accuracy and PH measures.
rows.measure: Temporal lag between test-accuracy changes and PH-statistic changes
rows.baseline: Whether PH changes precede or follow test-accuracy changes.
rows.value: A lag centered around 1,000 training steps; changes in test accuracy precede PH shifts.
rows.note: For this PH progress measure, the reported ordering is later rather than anticipatory.
rows.check: PH representation statistics are not the generalizing-circuit progress measures V2 names. V2 does not claim every statistic anticipates the jump, so 'reversed' against V2 is wrong. Moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Two-layer Transformer, modular addition, p = 197, α ∈ {0.2, 0.25, 0.3}, five seeds
relationships.reason: Training accuracy is near-perfect within a few thousand steps. Generalization comes at about 15k–20k steps for α = 0.3 versus 35k–45k for α = 0.2; grokking persists with up to 10% label permutation (r1, r2, r3, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy became nearly perfect within a few thousand steps, while generalization arrived around 15,000–20,000 steps with 30% training data versus 35,000–45,000 with 20%, persisting with up to 10% label permutation.
